clue.text: Eleven tiny creatures conceal settlement

parts.note: shrews are small insect-eating mammals
to bury something is to hide it away
a town is a settled community

explanation.surface: A colony of small animals hides away a village.
explanation.walkthrough: An eleven is a football team; SHREWSBURY TOWN is a professional English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side fields eleven players, so a named club can be called an eleven.

clue.text: Single sung very deep

indicators.note: something sung is voiced out loud, so the clue points to how a phrase sounds

parts.note: very deep is 'so low', which when spoken matches the answer

explanation.surface: A lone performer delivers a song in a very low register.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo is a single performance by one person, the sense of single as alone.

clue.text: Painter and trainee initially see you lifting tap

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock painter

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of trainee
in a down clue, lifting means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, like 'see you'

explanation.surface: An artist and an apprentice say goodbye while turning on a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-a-tat is a series of sharp knocks, which is a tapping sound.

clue.text: Boozers right sticking with one brewed in country local

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the name of the country

parts.note: Wales is the country next door to England, local to the UK

indicators.note: brewed suggests ingredients mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinkers are drawn to a beer brewed in a country pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' belongs to the country, not the pub: it is the country on England's doorstep. 'brewed' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozer is British slang for a pub, and watering holes is the jocular term for pubs too.

clue.text: Mass housing this type of terrier's found

definitions.meaning: Mass is short for Massachusetts, so the clue asks for a city within that US state
a small breed of dog with a tuxedo-like coat is named after the Massachusetts capital

explanation.surface: A church service is held where a certain breed of terrier lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a church service or a heap, but it is the abbreviation for Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Massachusetts shares its name with a recognised American terrier breed.

clue.text: Holiday centre in Sweden along the lines of bay

parts.note: a recess is a break, as when Parliament or a school stops sitting

indicators.note: centre in says take the middle letters of Sweden

explanation.surface: A vacation in the middle of Sweden is spent by a bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a hollow set back into a coast or wall, so shaped like one means set back.

clue.text: See 1
Senior citizen getting over land marginally steep

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: marginally says keep only the edge letters of land

parts.note: steep can mean expensive, the same as dear

explanation.surface: A pensioner gets across ground that is rather steep.
explanation.definitionFit: Old dear is a British informal and affectionate term for an elderly woman.

clue.text: One begins to work in north, upsetting strategist on the board

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the rearranged letters of north
upsetting means the letters of north are knocked into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
when a plan gels it starts to come together and work

explanation.surface: Someone starts a job in the North, which upsets a planner at the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges NORTH into NHORT, and I GELS goes 'in' it. Nigel Short is an English chess grandmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess grandmaster plans strategy across the chessboard, making him a strategist on the board.

clue.text: Figure of speech used by child captivated by tales

indicators.note: captivated by suggests one piece held inside another

parts.note: tales can be untruths, that is lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child uses a phrase while spellbound by stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is ironic understatement, saying 'not bad' for good: a rhetorical device.

clue.text: Georgians eat this fancy date dipped in eggy drink

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation like 'fancy that!'

indicators.note: dipped in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: nog, as in eggnog, is a drink made with eggs

explanation.surface: Something fancy, a date fruit, is dunked in eggnog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgians' are not Tbilisi residents but people of the US state of Georgia, where battered sausages on sticks are standard fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter-coated sausage on a stick is a common snack in the American South, including Georgia.

clue.text: Game's merchandise taken to fair somewhere in central London

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game, with the 's attached
to merchandise goods is to sell them
square means fair or honest, as in a square deal

explanation.surface: Goods from a game are carried to a market fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Russell Square is a garden square in Bloomsbury, London, also a London Underground station.
explanation.definitionFit: This Bloomsbury garden square is a place in central London, hence somewhere there.

clue.text: Mottled cat's a nightmare for slow animal?

parts.note: a tortoise is the proverbially slow animal, and the possessive gives its 's
hell is a nightmarish experience

explanation.surface: A speckled cat is a terror for a sluggish creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: the second half reads as a possessive phrase, the bad place belonging to the slow creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat with blotched black, orange and brown fur is called by this name.

clue.text: Note islands have to launch charity after revolution — it's shocking

indicators.note: after revolution says the whole string is turned round

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
CI stands for the Channel Islands
to lob is to toss or launch
aid is charitable help

explanation.surface: A memo notes that islanders must start a charity after an uprising, which is scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' turns the whole string round, not just the last piece; 'have' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something diabolical is appalling or outrageous, as is anything shocking.

clue.text: Fiancee regularly rejected outside union reception, finally agreeing

indicators.note: outside means the first letters wrap around the rest
regularly rejected means every other letter of fiancee is thrown out, keeping the even ones

parts.note: TU is a trade union

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of reception

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be keeps refusing a union party, but in the end she agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of Fiancee give INE, wrapped 'outside' TU and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in tune is to be in harmony or accord, as people agreeing are.

clue.text: Examination on part of body held in school

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: held in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the ear is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A medical exam of a body part is carried out at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is a close investigation of a subject, an examination of it.

clue.text: How a young kid might be stoned after joint

definitions.text: How a young kid might be

indicators.note: after puts the second piece following the first

parts.note: the knee is a joint
high is slang for intoxicated by drugs

explanation.surface: A child gets stoned after smoking a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' and 'stoned' tempt a drugs reading; the joint is the one in the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child stands only about as tall as an adult's knee.

clue.text: German musician entertains knight with flourish in court

indicators.note: entertains means one piece hosts another inside it

parts.note: Bach was a German composer
K is the chess abbreviation for knight
and means together with

explanation.surface: A German composer hosts a knight with great ceremony at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhand is a tennis stroke, a stroke played on the court.

clue.text: Horse left amongst hay worked on last?

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy horse

indicators.note: amongst means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: hay as in 'hit the hay' is bed

explanation.surface: A horse left among the hay was the last one worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbled means made or mended by a shoemaker, who shapes shoes on a last.

clue.text: High-reaching worker perhaps succeeded subsequently

parts.note: subsequently means later

explanation.surface: An ambitious employee eventually got ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer laying tiles works up high on roofs, hence high-reaching.

clue.text: One's occasionally filed work that's framed in French Academy

indicators.note: the work has the academy framed in it, one piece inside another

parts.note: toil is hard work
ENA is the Ecole Nationale d'Administration, an elite French school

explanation.surface: A document is occasionally filed at a French academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Toenails get trimmed with a nail file now and then.

clue.text: Run quickly, son — run off!

parts.note: to run off copies is to print them

explanation.surface: A parent urges their son to hurry away.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprint is to run at full speed over a short distance.

clue.text: Period of contentment in France that follows taking endless classified drug

indicators.note: follows puts this piece after the others
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: classified or tagged is labelled
EPO is a performance-enhancing drug
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A French era of happiness came after someone took a classified drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last D of LABELLED. La Belle Epoque was the comfortable era in France before the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the prosperous, settled years in France around 1900, a happy era.

clue.text: What's sold at number 3 stand, visibly empty

parts.note: to stand is to exist or be

indicators.note: empty means remove the middle, leaving the outer letters of visibly

explanation.surface: An empty-looking stall at number 3 is where things get sold.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 3 is 3 Down, the pubs; a bevy (usually bevvy) is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevy is British slang for an alcoholic drink, the stock in trade of pubs.

clue.text: This 1 Down clue somewhat misdirected heavyweights

indicators.note: misdirected means the letters run the wrong way, read backwards
somewhat means only a middle stretch of the combined string is kept, its outer letters trimmed away

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 1 Down is a single performance
taken as written

explanation.surface: This crossword clue is pointing solvers the wrong way towards big beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 Down' means its answer, written in among the clue's own words; 'somewhat' keeps ISSOLOC from the middle and 'misdirected' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are giants, people or things of huge size or importance.

clue.text: Being next to nothing, one has inside of gazebo floored

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
nada is Spanish for nothing

indicators.note: inside of takes the central letters of gazebo

explanation.surface: Next to nobody, someone has the gazebo floor laid.
explanation.definitionFit: Floored can mean stunned or bewildered, the state of someone dazed.

clue.text: Siren literally indicating gas leak, half ignored by female Yankee

parts.note: lady is a female title
to gas is to chat idly

indicators.note: half ignored means only the front half of the word leak is kept

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A siren signals a gas leak, partly overlooked by an American woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' hints at literary: the siren is from D H Lawrence's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence's heroine is a seductive woman of literature, a siren of the printed page.
